name: Selin-6-en-4α-ol

papers.title: Chemical composition and biological activities of an essential oil from the aerial parts of Artemisia Gmelinii weber ex Stechm

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

evidence: Measured in 1 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.07% of total volatiles (0.014mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Selin-6-en-4α-ol is a naturally occurring sesquiterpene alcohol, a class of aromatic compounds that give many plants their distinct scents and environmental defenses. It is typically encountered as a minor component in the fragrant essential oils of certain wild herbs.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the essential oil of the aerial parts of Artemisia gmelinii, a type of aromatic wormwood.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to selin-6-en-4α-ol to understand its contribution to the biological activity of Artemisia essential oils. Early computational work, such as molecular docking simulations, is exploring whether compounds in these oils might interact with enzymes related to blood sugar regulation and cognitive health. Currently, the evidence is limited to preliminary laboratory and computational models, with no clinical evidence found.

structure_function.statement: Selin-6-en-4α-ol is being studied for potential antioxidant properties.
structure_function.basis: This rests on a single paper evaluating the biological activities of an essential oil mixture containing the compound.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether selin-6-en-4α-ol contributes to the free-radical scavenging abilities of Artemisia essential oils. If this bears out, it could help explain the traditional uses of these aromatic plants.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: An in vitro study isolating selin-6-en-4α-ol to test its direct free-radical scavenging capacity using standard antioxidant assays, such as DPPH or ABTS, compared to known antioxidant controls.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: The current evidence is limited to preliminary computational and mixture-based laboratory studies, with no direct animal or human evidence found.
